intestateOrder.citation: Uniform Probate Code §2-102: the surviving spouse takes first. Model law the states follow in form; every state's intestacy statute puts the spouse first (Uniform Law Commission, Uniform Probate Code, 2019 text).
Uniform Probate Code §2-103(a)(1): with no surviving spouse, the decedent's descendants, by representation.
Uniform Probate Code §2-103(a)(2): with no descendant, the decedent's parents equally.
Uniform Probate Code §2-103(a)(3): with no parent, the descendants of the decedent's parents (siblings), by representation.

Uniform Probate Code §2-103(a)(4): grandparents and their descendants come next; grandchildren already take under §2-103(a)(1) as descendants when no child survives. The game records only these relations, so the two share the last kin class.
intestateOrder.estimatedFrom: UPC §2-103 order, collapsed to the relations the game records

escheat.citation: Uniform Probate Code §2-105: with no taker under the intestacy order, the estate passes to the state. Every state, D.C. and the five territories escheat an heirless estate to their own government; the details (which agency, how long it holds a claim) differ and are not modeled.
escheat.estimatedFrom: UPC §2-105; state escheat statutes, not compiled per place
